name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social media platforms, including the CLSB methodology, CooRnet/CooRTweet tools, and the VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most actively developed line of work.

name: Disinformation Narratives Monitoring
description: Monitoring and modeling the propagation of disinformation narratives across Europe on sensitive topics such as the war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, and elections, including dashboard and language-model tools built for fact-checkers and journalists (PROMPT project).

name: Platform Data Access & Research Methods
description: Methodological and infrastructural work on how researchers access, use, and are constrained by social media platform APIs and datasets (CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta URL Shares Dataset thresholds, DSA-era APIs, clean-room environments), a recurring concern for reproducible computational social science.

name: LLMs in Content Analysis
description: Integration and validation of large language models within content-analysis and annotation pipelines for political discourse and communication research, addressing challenges of embedding models, human-machine disagreement, and coding reliability.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Disinformation
description: Study of how generative AI is used to produce and evolve visual and textual persuasion in coordinated disinformation and scam campaigns (e.g., gambling promotion, deceptive information operations), and the countermeasures needed to detect them.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan communities, affective engagement, insularity, and polarization dynamics on social media platforms, spanning Italian, Brazilian, German and cross-national contexts, and their interplay with traditional media.

name: Italian Electoral Communication
description: Long-running empirical program (MINE) mapping Italian news media coverage, Facebook/Instagram interaction patterns, and coordinated networks around Italian elections (2018, 2019 European, 2022), the founding research line anchoring the researcher's academic identity.

name: Platform Governance & Content Moderation
description: Examination of platform policy changes and their effects on public discourse and political actors' visibility, such as Meta's political content reduction policy and shifts from open to 'walled garden' data ecosystems.

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Mapping coordinated networks that circulate problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration and cross-national studies in India and Nigeria examining local socio-political drivers of health misinformation.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.
